headline: Comcast splits off NBCUniversal as broadband keeps sliding
summary_short: Revenue was $29.94B (-1.2% y/y, +4.7% on a pro forma basis) and Adjusted EPS was $1.04 (-16.7% y/y), while GAAP EPS fell to $0.99 largely because Q2 2025 included a $9.4B pretax gain from the Hulu stake sale; Comcast also announced plans to spin off NBCUniversal and Sky into an independent public company.
summary_long: Revenue fell 1.2% y/y to $29.94B, though pro forma revenue (excluding Versant and the sold Sky Germany unit) rose 4.7%. Net income dropped to $3.53B from $11.12B mainly because the year-ago quarter included a $9.4B pretax gain on the Hulu stake sale; Adjusted EPS fell 16.7% to $1.04. Residential broadband kept losing customers (-167K) though the pace improved y/y, while domestic wireless added a record 448K lines and Business Services grew 3.7%. Peacock reached EBITDA profitability for the first time ($189M). Free cash flow was $4.6B; Comcast returned $2.1B to shareholders via dividends and buybacks, then paused repurchases after announcing plans to spin off NBCUniversal and Sky. Cash fell to $7.66B from $9.47B q/q on debt repayment.

drivers.explanation: Revenue decreased 1.2% y/y; on a pro forma basis excluding Versant and the divested Sky Germany operations, revenue rose 4.7%, reflecting underlying growth once separated businesses are stripped out.
Decline is mostly a comp issue: Q2 2025 net income included a $9.4B pretax ($7.1B after-tax) gain from the sale of Comcast's Hulu interest that did not recur this quarter.
Same driver as net income - EPS fell 66.8% y/y because the year-ago period's Hulu-sale gain added about $1.90 to prior-year EPS per the company's own reconciliation table.
EBITDA declined y/y as growth in Business Services Connectivity and Content & Experiences (Studios, Media) was more than offset by a decline in Residential Connectivity & Platforms EBITDA.

Per the six-month cash-flow statement, financing activities used $11.3B YTD - mainly $7.3B of net debt repayment, $2.5B of buybacks and $2.4B of dividends - which outpaced operating cash flow and drew the cash balance down.

Co-CEOs cited traction from the broadband go-to-market pivot, a record wireless quarter, continued Business Services growth and Peacock's first profitable quarter, alongside the newly announced plan to separate NBCUniversal and Sky into an independent public company.
